question: Should OpenClaw guarantee a child-visible warning before configured sub-agent deadlines, and should it be a built-in global behavior or a new configurable and per-spawn API surface?
rationale: Native control currently restarts the run while ACP has separate lifecycle semantics, so both the cross-runtime guarantee and the public configuration contract require maintainer intent.

options.title: Shared default warning
options.body: Add a non-destructive warning path with one conservative built-in interval and no per-spawn API expansion.

options.title: Config plus override
options.body: Add a global warning interval and per-spawn override after defining and proving equivalent native and ACP behavior.

options.title: No automatic warning
options.body: Keep hard deadlines and rely on explicit checkpoint instructions plus existing post-timeout recovery.

recommendation.title: Shared default warning
recommendation.body: Add a non-destructive warning path with one conservative built-in interval and no per-spawn API expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history most directly owns the shared timeout math, control lifecycle, and recent sub-agent architecture decisions.
